raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Syncs `rl/aux-output` with the latest remote `main` (`9a519c0585`) so the branch is no longer behind.

- Two merge commits bring in the 15 `main` commits the branch was missing (`40941f2c4b` first sync, then `9a519c0585` for the 3 newer ones).
- Preserves the branch-only design docs commit: `docs/design/rl_aux_output/*` (5 files, +642).
- After this PR, `git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main` is 0 and the only diff against `main` is that docs commit.

The PR shows 17 commits because a merge-based sync necessarily lists every `main` commit it brings into the branch (15) plus the 2 merge commits. The file diff is only `main`'s own changes; no code changes beyond the sync.

#### DCO note

The DCO check reports 9 commits from `main` with mismatched sign-off lines (squash-merged commits whose author is the GitHub login while `Signed-off-by` carries the real name/email). They are upstream commits, not part of this branch:

- `20ca5e8` anhtra3889, `33f68ea` aoshen02, `20f0890` bzsuni, `e11a5ad` Dilber, `8b30f56` Dilber, `3d18166` Juntian Liu (missing), `aa59a19` Park Soobin, `6124981` Tevin Shi, `a801d9e` Jaeyeong Choi (@Jaeyeong-CHOI).

`main` history is not GPG-signed and the repo has no `.github/dco.yml` remediation mode, so any PR that merges `main` into a branch hits this. Re-running the check will not change it; a maintainer override is the only fix.

@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+# Aux Outputs for RL
+
+RL trainers need per-token data that only the inference engine computes. This folder collects the design work on delivering those "aux outputs" from vLLM to the trainer at scale:
+
+- the experts each MoE layer routed to (R3, routing replay);
+- sparse-attention indexer selections;
+- top-k logprobs and the sampling support set;
+- the hidden state before `lm_head`, for full-vocabulary distillation.
+
+| Document | Contents |
+|---|---|
+| [Scenarios](scenarios.md) | Two sizing scenarios (single node, frontier-scale agentic RL) and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash measurements: bytes per token, cache and pool sizes, bandwidth, object counts |
+| [Protocol](protocol.md) | What the inference side, the training side, the engine and the store each do: request/response, object keys, read/release, in-flight cap, guarantees |
+| [Design space](design_space.md) | The design dimensions (cache segment, write granularity, keys, storage tiers, codecs) and the five end-to-end designs that were compared |
+| [Experiments](experiments.md) | Experiment matrix, setup, and results on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, with a status snapshot |
+
+## Requirements
+
+- **Requested means delivered.** If a request asks for an aux output, the trainer can read it. A full store makes the engine wait; it never drops rows.
+- **Freed once used.** Data is stored per session and deleted as soon as the session is consumed.
+
+## Conclusions so far
+
+1. **Split the problem in two.**
+   - *Cache segment*: rows for prefix-cache hits must live as long as the KV they belong to.
+   - *Delivery segment*: rows live from computation until the trainer has consumed them.
+2. **Delivery is written per block, keyed per session.**
+   - Each full KV block is written as soon as it fills, to `<job>/<session>/<block_hash>`.
+   - At request end the engine writes the tail and a manifest, and only then responds.
+   - A sample reads one manifest. Release deletes the session prefix in one call (0.2–1 ms).
+3. **"Requested means delivered" comes from flow control, not from dropping.**
+   - The writer retries until the write lands.
+   - The driver caps in-flight sessions so the pool cannot fill.
+   - A deadlock fallback aborts the newest sessions.
+   - Result: 0 missing rows and 0 leaked keys in every run, down to a 16 MB pool.
+4. **The first computation wins.**
+   - vLLM does not cache unfinished blocks, so the next turn re-prefills them, and that prefill can route a few rows differently from the decode that sampled those tokens.
+   - Keeping the rows the session already delivered made all five designs deliver rows bitwise equal to the engine's inline rows.
+5. **Rows for prefix hits should live and die with the KV.**
+   - An engine-local block-row cache allocated with the KV costs ~1% of the KV for R3 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (~1.6 GB per TP4 engine).
+   - Capping hits and recomputing only adds second computations.
+6. **Sizes on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.**
+   - R3: 480 B/token.
+   - Indexer: 16 KB/token raw, 2.5–3.6 KB after 20-bit packing and zstd.
+   - Hidden states: ~5 KB/token as fp8, with full-vocabulary KL < 1e-3.
+7. **Check batch invariance before relying on deduplication.** With `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, the sequence-parallel reduce-scatter was not batch-invariant on CUDA; it is fixed by a one-line change.
+
+## Status
+
+The delivery path and the experiments run as an overlay on a vLLM build (commit `da8922bf0f`) with Mooncake. Indexer and hidden-state delivery through the same path is in progress. Related RFCs:
+- #64380: delivery protocol;
+- #64383: R3 as a KV-cache layer.

@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+# Design Space
+
+The [protocol](protocol.md) is one point in this space. This page lays out the dimensions, the candidates, and why the protocol picks what it picks. Measurements are in [experiments](experiments.md); sizes in [scenarios](scenarios.md).
+
+## Two segments
+
+- **Cache segment**: for positions served by a prefix-cache hit, the rows must exist as long as the KV they belong to. Only outputs recorded at every position need one (R3, indexer, and hidden states when a teacher scores a student's tokens as prompt).
+- **Delivery segment**: from the moment rows are computed until the trainer has consumed them. Every output needs one.
+
+| Output | Positions | Cache segment? | Bytes/token (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) | Can the trainer recompute it instead? |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | all | yes | 480 B | no, it must match the rollout's routing |
+| top-k + mask | generated | no | 2 KB + ≤ 1 KB | no, it is the sampling-time distribution |
+| indexer | all | yes | 16 KB raw, 2.5–3.6 KB compressed | only under BI with the same weights |
+| hidden (full-vocab distillation) | positions the student is trained on | when they are prompt positions of a teacher request | 10 KB bf16, ~5 KB fp8 | no, the trainer has no teacher forward |
+
+## Cache segment: where rows for prefix hits come from
+
+| Option | Approach | Assessment |
+|---|---|---|
+| C0 | No cache segment; cap hits at `aux_start` and recompute the rest | Simplest. GRPO siblings lose prefix sharing (35% throughput loss measured on a 30B MoE). Recomputation creates second computations of the same positions (see "first computation wins"). |
+| C1 | Engine-local block-row cache, allocated and evicted with the KV; blocks missing from the session are written at request end | Chosen. ~1% of the KV for R3 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Every design delivered exact rows with it. |
+| C2 | R3 as an extra KV-cache layer (RFC #64383) | "KV hit ⇒ rows present" across all KV tiers, including offload. On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash it cost 0.21% of KV capacity. Needs a host for the layer in hybrid KV groups. |
+| C3 | Store keyed by global block hash (#57968) | Single copy; but release by batch loses rows still shared by other sessions, and pool pressure silently drops them. |
+| C4 | Extra room in GPU KV pages | Spends GPU KV; not recommended. |
+| C5 | C1 + C2: a capped KV layer with truncation beyond it | Correct but degrades to C0 behavior when full. |
+| C6 | The delivery pool doubles as the session's cache: allow a hit only if this session already published the block | No extra memory. Same-trajectory, fork and GRPO-sibling hits are covered; cross-session hits (shared system prompts) are truncated, costing <1% of prefill at frontier scale. |
+
+### Which prefix hits need a cache segment in RL
+
+1. **Next turn of the same trajectory.** These hits are within `aux_start`; the rows were already delivered.
+2. **Forks and tree search.** Under session-scoped keys the parent's rows already sit in the delivery pool, pinned until the session is released.
+3. **GRPO siblings.** Treat the group as one session (or use one `n>1` request), and they become case 2.
+4. **Across sessions** (a common system prompt). Only these need a real cache segment, and truncating them costs little.
+
+## Delivery segment
+
+### Write granularity
+
+| Option | Approach | Assessment |
+|---|---|---|
+| W0 | Write everything at request end | Rejected: a write spike at the end, the response waits, host memory is unbounded. |
+| W1 | Write each full KV block when it fills | Chosen for KV-following outputs; aligns with session-scoped block keys. |
+| W2 | Batch N blocks per object (1–4 MB) | 16–128× fewer objects; rows sit longer in host memory. An option if object rate becomes a limit. |
+| W3 | Chunk sampling-following outputs by generated tokens | Chosen for top-k, mask and hidden states. |
+
+### Keys and deduplication scope
+
+| Option | Key | Deduplication | Release |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| K1 | per request, plus `aux_start` from the client | within a trajectory | per batch, no counting |
+| K2 | per session: `<session>/<block_hash>` | within a trajectory tree, without client bookkeeping | delete the session prefix |
+| K3 | global block hash | across trajectories | cannot release per batch without reference counting (rows were lost when tried) |
+
+K2 is chosen. Cross-trajectory sharing (common system prompts) is worth ~0.24 GB per node for R3: not worth reference counting.
+
+### Data path
+
+- GPU → host → background put: the current path, used in the experiments.
+- With R3 as a KV layer, rows are already in host memory and can be put directly when a block fills.
+- GPU staging → RDMA put: the candidate for the indexer.
+
+### Storage tiers
+
+- **Host DRAM pool** (Mooncake segments): R3, top-k, mask, compressed indexer, fp8 hidden.
+- **NVMe/SSD**: the overflow tier for indexer and hidden states.
+- **Shared-filesystem copy-out**: once a trajectory finishes, copy its blocks to packed files and delete them from the pool. This shrinks the pool and survives trainer checkpoint restore, at the cost of an extra read and write. Cluster-wide write load is ~7 GB/s without the indexer and ~90 GB/s with it.
+
+### Encodings
+
+- R3: uint16 ids (384 experts), or 9-bit packing for a 44% saving.
+- Top-k: 17-bit ids plus bf16 logprobs. Mask: CSR.
+- Indexer: 20-bit packing plus zstd (measured 4.6–6.7×). Delta encoding does not help on top of zstd.
+- Hidden: fp8 with a per-token scale.
+- Every field carries a codec name.
+
+### Requested means delivered
+
+1. Backpressure: retry until the write lands, never time out. The engine pauses scheduling when pending bytes exceed a cap.
+2. An in-flight cap at the trajectory or group level: `C ≈ 0.75 × pool / max session bytes`. Start from a conservative bound and only lower it from observed sizes. The indexer makes sessions large, which is why it must be compressed or tiered.
+3. Deadlock fallback: abort the newest sessions and regenerate them.
+
+### Freed once used
+
+- Delete the session prefix after the step commits, or after copy-out.
+- After each weight sync, sweep generations older than the oldest live trajectory.
+- The engine deletes request-private objects of undeliverable responses.
+- Report the number of keys swept at job end as a leak metric.
+
+### Correctness corner cases
+
+- **First computation wins.** vLLM does not cache unfinished blocks, so the next turn re-prefills `[unfinished block start, aux_start)`. A prefill resuming after a cache hit can route a few rows differently from the decode that sampled those tokens. Keep the rows the session already delivered.
+- **Preemption.** A recomputed block rewrites the same key with the same bytes (under BI).
+- **MTP rejection.** Rows of rejected tokens are dropped.
+- **Stop strings.** The tail is truncated.
+- **Prefill/decode disaggregation.** Both sides must use the same block-hash configuration.
+- **Multimodal prompts.** Block hashes include image hashes.
+- **Weight sync.** `reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)` with R3 on must not crash the engine.
+- **R3 as a KV layer on hybrid KV groups.** Attach the layer to a group with one slot per token (compression ratio 1).
+
+### Hidden states for full-vocabulary distillation
+
+- Take the `lm_head` input: after the final hyper-connection merge and final norm. Any other tensor makes the trainer's logits mismatch.
+- Positions:
+  - If the teacher scores the student's tokens by prefill, those are prompt positions of the teacher request. They follow the KV and get prefix hits, the same as R3.
+  - If the teacher is the rollout model, they are generated positions.
+- Training side: read the hidden states, multiply by the teacher's `lm_head` sharded by vocabulary across TP, and never gather full logits on one rank.
+
+## The five designs compared
+
+All five share the same delivery segment: W1/W3 writes, K2 keys, backpressure, the in-flight cap, and session release. They differ in the cache segment.
+
+| Design | R3 cache segment | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| c1 | C1: engine-local block-row cache tied to the KV, with missing blocks back-filled into the session | Exact |
+| c0 | C0: cap hits at `aux_start` | Exact after "first computation wins". Loses prefix sharing for GRPO siblings. |
+| P-S | C6: the delivery pool as the session cache | Exact after "first computation wins". Output tokens differ from other designs because hit patterns differ. |
+| P-B | C2: R3 as a KV-cache layer (on the GPU in this port; 0.21% of KV) | Exact after "first computation wins" |
+| P-A | C3: global block hash (#57968), keys-only response | Rows identical to c1 for all requests. Release semantics are unresolved for shared blocks. |
+
+### How each design fails the requirements
+
+| Failure | c1 / c0 / P-S / P-B | P-A |
+|---|---|---|
+| Delivery pool full | Backpressure; nothing dropped | Cache objects and delivery objects are the same copy. They can be neither evicted (pinned) nor deleted (still hit), so the pool can only back-pressure. |
+| Writer process dies | Only that process's undelivered rows are lost; the driver regenerates the trajectory | Every engine sharing that prefix loses the rows |
+| Trainer is done | Delete the session; space returns immediately | Blocks may still be hit by other sessions; deleting them causes missing rows, so this needs reference counting or a pool that only grows |
+
+## Not adopted
+
+- **Write at request end, hard-pin forever, fail the request on write errors** (the SGLang output-store approach): equivalent to C0 + W0 + K1. Its good parts are kept:
+  - self-describing references;
+  - all-or-nothing writes;
+  - the engine deleting undeliverable objects;
+  - codecs;
+  - pre-registered read buffers.
+- **Distributed reference counting:** the driver already knows when a session is consumed.
+- **Engine-side admission:** the engine cannot tell a new trajectory from the next turn of an old one, so blocking the latter deadlocks.
+- **Per-field keys:** they multiply master operations by 3–5×; range reads within one object achieve the same.

+# Aux Output Experiments
+
+End-to-end measurements behind the [protocol](protocol.md). The designs are described in [design space](design_space.md).
+
+## Experiment matrix
+
+| ID | What | Pass criterion |
+|---|---|---|
+| X0 | Model output sanity; KV token capacity and bytes per token; where an R3 KV layer can attach | Correct, diverse outputs; real capacity numbers |
+| X1 | Correctness per design: multi-turn agent, GRPO and forks; delivered rows vs inline rows | 0 missing, 0 wrong |
+| X1b | Row determinism across schedules: the same prompt alone, as 8 copies, mixed with long prompts, decode vs re-prefill | Bitwise identical |
+| X2 | Throughput with aux outputs on | Measured per design |
+| X3 | Host memory and pool peaks | Extrapolated to frontier scale |
+| X4 | Requested means delivered: small pool, continuous sessions | 0 missing, no deadlock |
+| X5 | Freed once used: release latency, leaks at the end | 0 leaks |
+| X6 | Indexer compression on real selections | Ratio and codec speed |
+| X7 | Hidden states: recomputed logits vs vLLM, fp8 error on full-vocab KL | Choose bf16 or fp8 |
+| X9 | Trainer-side logprob recompute with R3 replay from the connector (forward only) | Rows aligned; replay effect measured |
+
+## Status snapshot
+
+| ID | c1 | c0 | P-S | P-B | P-A | Shared |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| X0 | | | | | | pass |
+| X1 | pass | pass in X4 (not rerun as X1) | pass | pass | pass (hashes equal to c1) | |
+| X1b | | | | | | `auto` pass; `deep_gemm_mega_moe` fail, fixed |
+| X4/X5 | pass | pass | pass | — | — | |
+| X6 | | | | | | pass |
+| X7 | | | | | | pass |
+| X9 | | | | | | pass (alignment verified) |
+| Indexer/hidden through the delivery path | | | pass | | | |
+
+## Setup
+
+- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (40 layers + 3 MTP, 384 experts with top-6, 8 indexer source layers with top-512), public config.
+- vLLM at commit `da8922bf0f`, Model Runner V2, one node with 4× GB200, TP4 + EP4.
+- Batch invariance on: `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, with `VLLM_BI_MXFP8_GEMM=tensor_core`, `VLLM_BI_MXFP8_PREQUANT=1`, `VLLM_BI_BF16_GEMM=tensor_core`.
+- Engine arguments: `kv_cache_dtype=nvfp4_ds_mla`, `attention_backend=FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, prefix caching on. MoE backend `auto` (resolves to `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`) unless noted.
+- Store: one Mooncake master plus one segment holder on the same node.
+- Delivery: block-wise writes keyed by `<job>/<session>/<block_hash>`, a tail and a manifest at request end, and release by session prefix. The delivery path was implemented on top of the block-keyed aux output connector (#45635).
+- Workloads (X1):
+  - multi-turn agent, 16 sessions × 4 turns;
+  - GRPO, 4 groups × 8;
+  - forks: 8 parents and 8 children.
+
+  That is 112 requests in total. Each request is checked three ways:
+  - **delivered**: rows read back through the manifest;
+  - **inline**: rows returned by the engine;
+  - **reference**: a no-cache full prefill.
+
+## Designs compared
+
+All designs share the delivery path. They differ in where rows for prefix-cache hits come from:
+
+| Design | Rows for prefix-cache hits come from |
+|---|---|
+| c1 | an engine-local block-row cache, allocated and evicted with the KV; blocks missing from the session are written at request end |
+| c0 | nowhere: prefix hits are capped at `aux_start` and recomputed |
+| P-S | the delivery pool doubles as the session's cache: hits are capped at the longest prefix this session already published |
+| P-B | R3 is an extra KV-cache layer (RFC #64383) |
+| P-A | Mooncake keyed by the global block hash (#57968), keys-only output |
+
+## Results
+
+### Capacity
+
+- KV capacity of a TP4 engine at 0.65 GPU memory utilization: 3.39M tokens.
+- A block-row cache sized to the KV:
+  - R3: ~1.6 GB per engine (~1% of the KV);
+  - indexer: ~54 GB raw, ~10 GB compressed.
+- P-B (R3 as a KV layer) reduced KV capacity by 0.21%.
+
+### Correctness (X1)
+
+With the "first computation wins" rule:
+
+| Design | Missing rows | Delivered = inline | Left after release |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| c1 | 0 | 112/112 | 0 |
+| P-S | 0 | 112/112 | 0 |
+| P-B | 0 | 112/112 | 0 |
+| P-A | 0 | 112/112 (R3 row hashes equal to c1 for all 112 requests) | 0 |
+
+Without that rule, c0, P-B and c1 each had a few requests where 1–177 rows differed. The rows were exactly `[start of the last unfinished block, aux_start)`, re-prefilled by the next turn after a prefix hit.
+
+A full prefill from position 0 matched decode bitwise in these tests. A prefill resuming after a cache hit did not always match. For the same reason, generated tokens can differ between designs (41/112 between P-S and c1): each design changes the hit pattern, and the output depends on where a prefill resumes. Within each run, delivery was exact.
+
+### Always delivered, freed after use (X4/X5)
+
+The workload was 96 sessions × 4 turns. The trainer reads each finished session and then releases it.
+
+| Design | Pool | In-flight cap | Missing | Wrong | Leaked keys | Release p50 |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| c1 | 64 MB | 46 sessions | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.4 ms |
+| c0 | 64 MB | 46 sessions | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.4 ms |
+| P-S | 64 MB | 46 sessions | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.3 ms |
+| P-S | 16 MB | 11 sessions | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.2 ms |
+
+The in-flight cap kept the pool from ever filling, so backpressure never triggered.
+
+### Throughput
+
+Output tokens/s for X1 (agent / GRPO / fork):
+
+| Design | Agent | GRPO | Fork |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| c1 | 654 | 474 | 321 |
+| P-S | 624 | 428 | 348 |
+| P-B | 675 | 394 | 375 |
+| P-A | 662 | 434 | 353 |
+
+The workload is small, and the differences are within run-to-run noise.
+
+### Indexer replay (X6)
+
+- Selections are bitwise identical across runs under batch invariance.
+- Raw size: 8 layers × 512 × int32 = 16 KB/token.
+
+| Encoding | Size per token | Ratio |
+|---|---|---|
+| 20-bit packing | 10 KB | 1.6× |
+| zstd-3 | — | 4.5–6.1× |
+| 20-bit packing + zstd-3 | 2.5–3.6 KB | 4.6–6.7× |
+
+- Codec speed: 300–380 MB/s per core.
+- Delta encoding on top of zstd does not help.
+
+### Indexer and hidden states through the delivery path
+
+Indexer selections and hidden states were added to the same block-wise path as R3, with the P-S design on 112 requests:
+- indexer: one object per full block, 20-bit packing + zstd, same deduplication and "first computation wins" rule as R3;
+- hidden states: one object per 64 generated positions, fp8 e4m3 with a per-token scale;
+- the manifest describes every field.
+
+| Output | Check | Result | Bytes stored per token |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | delivered vs inline rows | 112/112 equal, 0 missing | 480 (raw) |
+| Indexer | delivered vs an independent in-engine capture of the same requests | 112/112 bitwise equal, 0 missing, 0 holes | 551 (16,384 raw) |
+| Hidden | delivered vs the captured hidden state | every row is the exact fp8 requantization | 5,124 (10,240 as bf16) |
+
+Stored indexer bytes are far below the per-token compressed size (2.5–3.6 KB) because blocks are written once per session.
+
+Full-vocabulary check for hidden states: the delivered fp8 hidden state times `lm_head`, compared with vLLM's distribution.
+
+| Metric | Mean | Max |
+|---|---|---|
+| KL | 7.7e-4 | 0.012 |
+| Logprob difference | 0.019 | 0.24 |
+
+All objects were removed by session release, with 0 keys left.
+
+**Throughput.** Total output tokens/s over 4 alternating passes per arm (first pass excluded as warm-up):
+
+| Arm | Median | Range |
+|---|---|---|
+| R3 only | 552 | 520–565 |
+| R3 + indexer + hidden | 495 | 443–533 |
+
+That is ~10% lower. The ranges overlap on this small workload, and the split between compression, device-to-host copies and puts has not been measured.
+
+### Hidden states (X7)
+
+| Comparison | Result |
+|---|---|
+| fp32 `lm_head(hidden)` vs vLLM logits | max abs diff 2.1e-4; not bitwise |
+| bf16 `lm_head(hidden)` vs vLLM logits | max abs diff 0.062 |
+| fp8 e4m3 with a per-token scale | full-vocabulary KL mean 4.4e-4 / 8.7e-4, max 1.9e-3 / 2.8e-3; argmax agreement 98–100% |
+
+### Trainer-side logprob recompute with replay (X9)
+
+R3 rows for 16 sessions were read back from the connector and replayed in a BF16 trainer (TP1/EP16), forward only, with no optimizer and no gradients.
+
+- **Alignment check:** the fraction of tokens whose expert set differs between trainer and rollout is:
+  - 2% at layer 0 when aligned;
+  - ~100% when shifted by ±1 position or compared against the wrong layer.
+- **Real routing gap:** quantized rollout vs BF16 trainer grows with depth: 16% at layer 1, 40–85% in deep layers.
+- **Effect of replay on trainer logprobs:**
+
+| | Mean abs diff | Max abs diff |
+|---|---|---|
+| Replay off | 0.175 | 8.15 |
+| Replay on | 0.082 | 3.09 |
+
+## Finding: `deep_gemm_mega_moe` broke batch invariance
+
+With `moe_backend="deep_gemm_mega_moe"`, the same prompt run alone vs batched gave different R3 rows and different greedy tokens. The backend enables MoE sequence parallelism: each TP rank owns a 1/TP slice of the step's tokens, and attention partial sums are combined with a reduce-scatter. On CUDA under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the batch-invariant branch of `CudaCommunicator.reduce_scatter` is gated on `current_platform.is_rocm()`, so the call falls through to a plain NCCL ring reduce-scatter, whose summation order depends on which rank owns the output slice. A token's attention output therefore depends on which slice it lands in. Per-layer instrumentation confirms it: the four per-rank inputs to the layer-0 post-attention reduce-scatter are bitwise equal while its output is not; growing the batch with the probe token on the same rank changes nothing. Dropping the `is_rocm()` condition (so CUDA uses `reduce_scatter_batch_invariant`) makes alone / 8 copies / mixed batches bitwise identical in R3 rows, greedy tokens and logprobs. The cost of the extra all-to-all is not measured; any configuration that enables MoE sequence parallelism (e.g. DP>1 with TP>1 and EP) should be affected.
+
+## Bugs found while building the delivery path
+
+- **Manifest deferred to the next engine step:** an idle offline engine never wrote it. Write it when the request finishes.
+- **Keys built from the engine-internal request id:** the id has a random suffix, so the caller could not find the objects. Use the caller-visible id.
+- **Duplicate puts from every TP rank retried forever:** treat "key already exists" as success.
+- **One extra row:** async scheduling runs a forward for the last sampled token. Readers truncate to `L−1`.
+- **Replay hook bypassed in the trainer:** some MoE implementations call `route` directly, bypassing a router-level replay hook. Hook replay at the call that computes routing.

+# Aux Outputs for RL: Delivery Protocol
+
+Status: draft (v3.9). Measurements behind each rule are in [experiments](experiments.md); sizes in [scenarios](scenarios.md); alternatives in [design space](design_space.md).
+
+RL trainers need per-token data that only the inference engine computes: the experts each MoE layer routed to (R3, for routing replay), sparse-attention indexer selections, top-k logprobs, the sampling support set, and the last hidden state before `lm_head` (for full-vocabulary distillation). This document specifies how vLLM delivers these "aux outputs" to the trainer at scale: who writes what, where, when, and who frees it.
+
+## Principles
+
+1. **Requested means delivered.** If a request asks for an aux output, the trainer can read it. A full store makes the engine wait; it never drops rows or gives up on a write.
+2. **Freed once used.** Objects are stored per session (consumption unit). The driver deletes a whole session once it is consumed and the training step has committed. No distributed reference counting. The store only reclaims expired objects as a backstop.
+3. **Written per block; the reference comes last.** Each full KV block's rows are written as soon as the block completes. At request end, the tail and a small manifest are written, and only then is the final response (carrying the manifest reference) sent. Every reference the client sees points at objects that already exist.
+4. **The first computation wins.** A position's rows come from the first forward that computed it; for generated tokens, that is the forward whose logits sampled the next token. vLLM does not cache unfinished blocks, so the next turn re-prefills `[start of the unfinished block, aux_start)`. That prefill can route a few rows differently even with batch invariance on. Rows the session already delivered are kept; the recomputation never overwrites them.
+
+## Outputs
+
+| Output | Follows | Positions | Bytes/token (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) | Use |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `routed_experts` (R3) | KV | all | 40 layers × 6 × uint16 = 480 B | routing replay in the trainer |
+| `indexer_topk` | KV | all | 8 layers × 512 × 20 bit, zstd: ~2.5–3.6 KB (16 KB raw) | sparse-attention replay |
+| `topk_logprobs` | sampling | generated | k × 8 B | truncated distillation, KL |
+| `sampling_mask` | sampling | generated | CSR, ≤ 256 ids per row | reconstruct the truncated/masked support |
+| `hidden_states` | sampling | generated | `lm_head` input, fp8 + per-token scale, ~5 KB | full-vocabulary student training |
+
+- The sampled token's logprob is not stored; it is returned inline with the response (per-token logprobs in `processed_logprobs` mode). That number is the behavior probability.
+- fp8 hidden states multiplied by the teacher's `lm_head` give a full-vocabulary distribution within KL < 1e-3 of vLLM's (argmax agreement 98–100%). Recomputing logits from hidden states is not bitwise equal to vLLM's logits (max diff 2e-4 even in fp32), so trainers must not expect to reproduce the behavior logprob from hidden states.
+
+**Position convention.** Row `p` belongs to position `p`: the position that processes token `p` and produces the logits for token `p+1`. KV-following outputs have a row at every position. Sampling-following outputs have a row only where `p+1` is a token generated by this request, i.e. `p ∈ [P−1, P+O−1)` for prompt length `P` and output length `O`. Positions are counted on the engine-side sequence (after multimodal expansion); responses always return the engine-side `prompt_token_ids`.
+
+## Inference side
+
+### Request
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `aux_outputs` | Which outputs to produce. Absent means none. |
+| `aux_session` | The session (consumption unit) the request belongs to: a GRPO group, a trajectory tree, a multi-turn agent trajectory. All its objects share one key prefix and are released together. |
+| `aux_start` | "I already have the first `aux_start` rows of this sequence." Needed only for sampling-following outputs and inline mode; KV-following outputs are deduplicated per block within the session. |
+
+Sampling-parameter constraints (when requesting `topk_logprobs`, `sampling_mask` or `hidden_states`): temperature, `top_k`, `top_p`, `min_p` and token-masking parameters (guided decoding, `allowed_token_ids`, `bad_words`) are allowed; with any truncation or masking, `top_k ≤ 256` is required; parameters that change logit values (repetition/frequency/presence penalties, `logit_bias`) are rejected because the trainer cannot reconstruct them.
+
+### Response
+
+```json
+"prompt_token_ids": [...],
+"aux": {
+  "status": "ok",
+  "manifest": {"backend": "mooncake", "key": "<job>/<session>/<req>/m", "nbytes": 2380}
+}
+```
+
+- `status` is always present when `aux_outputs` was requested. It is `unavailable` only if the store itself is unreachable; a full store makes the engine wait instead. A response without `aux` to a request that asked for it is an error, not "no data" (e.g. a router dropped the field).
+- `<req>` is the caller-visible request id. Engine-internal ids carry a random suffix and must not be used in keys.
+- The **manifest** is a small self-describing object covering the whole sequence `[0, P+O−1)`, not just this request's new rows: the ordered block keys (shared within the session), the generated-chunk keys, the tail key, each field's name, dtype, per-token shape and codec, the total row count, and the tokens of each block (for verification). A training sample reads exactly one manifest, that of its leaf request.
+- **Inline mode** (small scale): the data is returned in the response, nothing is written to a store, and release is a no-op.
+
+### Objects
+
+- **Block** `<job>/<session>/<block_hash>`: all KV-following outputs for one full KV block, plus the block's tokens. Written when the block fills. Deduplicated within the session by block hash.
+- **Generated chunk** `<job>/<session>/<req>/g/<i>`: sampling-following outputs, one object per `block_size` generated positions.
+- **Tail** `<job>/<session>/<req>/t`: rows of the last, unfinished block, written at request end.
+- **Manifest** `<job>/<session>/<req>/m`: written at request end, after the tail and before the response.
+- Objects are immutable. Block hashes are vLLM's prefix block hashes (including multimodal, LoRA and `cache_salt` extra keys), so a key's content depends only on its full prefix.
+
+### Next request
+
+Multi-turn continuations, forks and GRPO siblings use the same `aux_session`; blocks already written are reused, not rewritten. A turn that switches policy or adapter uses a new session (same tokens, different routing; the block hash also includes the adapter name).
+
+## Training side
+
+```python
+rows = aux.read(manifest_ref, kind="routed_experts", layers=range(l0, l1), tokens=sample_tokens)
+...
+aux.release_session(job, session)  # after the session is consumed and the step committed
+```
+
+`aux` is a small standalone package (no vLLM or torch dependency) returning numpy arrays.
+
+- **read**
+  - Reads the manifest, then the blocks, generated chunks and tail; returns rows covering `[0, L−1)`.
+  - The manifest may report one row more than `L−1`: async scheduling runs one forward for the last sampled token before the request is known to be finished. `read` always truncates to `L−1`.
+  - Verifies each block's tokens against the sample; a mismatch is an error.
+  - R3 sanity: the 6 expert ids in a row are distinct; an all-zero row (the engine never saw the routing) is an error.
+  - Expert order within a row is not sorted. Replay compares sets; rows whose set is unchanged keep the trainer's own ids and weights.
+  - No waiting: a manifest implies all its objects exist. A failed read (store node down) fails the whole step; all ranks read, all-reduce a success flag, and retry or skip together.
+- **release**: deletes everything under `<job>/<session>/` (Mooncake `remove_by_regex` with force). Immediate and idempotent. The driver calls it once the session will not grow, all planned reads are done, and the step that used it has committed on all ranks. Dropped samples are not released individually; their blocks may be shared.
+- Retrying a failed step re-reads (nothing was released). Rolling back to an earlier checkpoint requires regeneration. Saving rollout data offline requires reading it inline first.
+
+## Driver
+
+1. **In-flight cap** (keeps "requested means delivered" from deadlocking): admit at most `C` concurrent sessions with `C × max_session_bytes ≤ 0.75 × pool`, where `max_session_bytes = longest context × bytes/token × branching factor`. New sessions wait for a slot; the next turn of an admitted session is always admitted (blocking it could deadlock). Count bytes, not requests. With several policies sharing a pool, cap each policy separately.
+2. **Release timing**: as above, after the step commits.
+
+**Deadlock fallback**: the cap is computed for the worst case, so the pool should never fill. If it does and no session completes for a while (default 60 s), the driver aborts the most recently admitted sessions, deletes their objects and regenerates those samples. The engine never drops rows on its own.
+
+## Engine and store guarantees
+
+**Where rows come from**
+
+- KV-following rows live and die with the KV. On a prefix-cache hit, a block's rows come from an engine-local block-row cache allocated and evicted together with the KV (sized to the KV token capacity; R3 on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is ~1.6 GB per TP4 engine, ~1% of the KV). Positions computed by this request take rows from this request's forward.
+- A block present in the local block-row cache but not yet written for this session (another session computed that prefix first) is written into this session at request end.
+- **First computation wins** (principle 4): when publishing a block, back-filling a block or writing a tail, positions before `aux_start` that this session already delivered take the rows from the session's previous tail. The worker remembers each session's last tail (start and rows) and overwrites those positions when a later write starts at the same position.
+- Do not cap prefix hits at `aux_start` to regenerate rows: capping only creates more second computations. If the block-row cache does not fit, offload rows with the KV (make the row cache a KV layer) rather than capping.
+- A no-cache full-prefill recomputation is not a correctness reference; it may legitimately differ from the first computation. The check is that inline rows (returned by the engine, first computation) equal the rows read back.
+- Session-level dedup by block hash assumes rows for a block are bitwise identical regardless of scheduling. Verify the deployment before relying on it: the same prompt run alone, as 8 identical copies in one batch, and mixed with long prompts must give identical rows.
+- Backends that cannot expose routing (fused kernels that bypass top-k) must reject R3 at startup.
+
+**Writes**
+
+- Each full block is written from a background thread in the worker, without blocking the forward.
+- All TP ranks compute identical rows. Have one rank write; if several do, "key already exists" counts as success (otherwise retries spin forever).
+- **On a full pool, retry until the write lands** (backpressure). Each worker caps its pending bytes; beyond the cap, the engine stops scheduling new tokens until writes catch up.
+- **Write the tail and manifest as soon as the request finishes.** Do not defer them to a later engine step: an idle engine never runs one.
+- Before responding, the engine deletes the request-private objects (tail, generated chunks, manifest) of responses that cannot be delivered. Session-shared blocks are left to session release.
+
+**Retention**
+
+- Objects are written with soft pin + TTL and the master configured with `allow_evict_soft_pinned_objects=false`: never evicted within the TTL, reclaimable afterwards when space is needed.
+- TTL ≥ longest session lifetime + batching and queueing time + margin. The master's eviction high watermark ≤ in-flight cap − one session's maximum bytes.
+- Objects are deleted only by the engine (undeliverable responses), by driver session release, or by expiry.
+- At normal job end, delete everything under `<job>/` and report the number of keys deleted as a leak metric; it should be 0.
+
+## Framework checklist
+
+Inference side:
+1. Send `aux_outputs` and `aux_session` with every request (one session per consumption unit; a new session when the policy changes).
+2. Store `prompt_token_ids`, the manifest reference, the generated tokens and the inline sampled logprobs in the sample.
+3. Treat a missing `aux` as an error.
+
+Training side:
+1. Carry the manifest reference through shuffling, packing and rank sharding.
+2. Keep the in-flight cap; call `release_session` after the step commits.
+3. Each rank reads its own fields, layers and positions, truncated to `L−1`; handle read failures collectively.
+4. Hook R3 replay where the model actually computes routing. For example, some MoE implementations call `route` directly and bypass a router-level replay hook.
+5. Read inline before saving rollouts offline.
+
+## Scenarios
+
+| Scenario | Inference side | Training side | Notes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Single-turn GRPO | n requests, one session | each sample reads its manifest; release the group | prompt blocks stored once |
+| Multi-turn agent | same session every turn | read the last turn's manifest; it covers the whole sequence | each turn writes only new blocks |
+| Framework trims trailing tokens | same session | read the new manifest | trimmed positions are not in it |
+| Forks / tree search | same session | each leaf reads its manifest; release the tree | parent blocks shared |
+| Context rewriting / compaction | same session | read the new manifest | rewritten prefixes hash differently and are rewritten |
+| Multiple policies / LoRAs | new session per policy | separate in-flight caps | block hash includes the adapter |
+| Abort and resume | a normal abort still writes a manifest for the computed positions | — | hard-cancelled requests' objects are deleted by the engine |
+| Full pool | writer blocks, engine pauses scheduling | in-flight cap makes this rare; deadlock fallback aborts the newest sessions | no rows dropped |
+| Cross-session prefix hit | — | — | rows come from the local block-row cache and are written into the session |
+| Pipeline / context / tensor parallel trainer | — | each rank reads its own fields, layers and positions | — |
+| Job end | — | delete by job prefix and report the count | expected 0 |

+# Sizing Scenarios
+
+Two scenarios bound the design: a single-node setup and a frontier-scale agentic RL run. All numbers assume batch invariance (BI) is on. Sizes come from model configs and formulas; assumptions are marked. The last section replaces the per-token sizes with measurements on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
+
+## 1. Scenarios
+
+| | Single node | Frontier scale |
+|---|---|---|
+| Model | Qwen3-30B-A3B | a ~500B-A23B MoE (49 MoE layers, 256 experts, 1M context) |
+| Workload | GRPO, short multi-turn agents | long-horizon agents with sub-agent forks |
+| Mean / max context | 16K / 32K (assumed) | 200K (assumed) / 1M |
+| Share of generated tokens | 50% (assumed) | 10%; multi-turn agents are prefill-dominated (assumed) |
+| Trajectories in flight (cluster) | 256 (assumed) | ≈110,000 (public report) |
+| In flight per replica | 32 (8 engines) | ≈51 (110,000 ÷ 2,160 replicas) |
+| Staleness | 0 to a few steps | up to ~107 weight versions (~1 day) |
+| Weight-sync interval | every step | ≈807 s (86,400 s ÷ 107) |
+| Inference | 1 node × 8 H200, 8 engines (TP1) | ≈2,160 GB300 nodes, one replica each (assumed) |
+| Training | colocated | ≈465 GB300 nodes (inference : training ≈ 4.65 : 1) |
+| Completion rate | — | ≈41 trajectories/s |
+
+By Little's law, a frontier-scale trajectory lives ≈110,000 ÷ 41.3 ≈ 2,660 s and spans about 3 weight updates.
+
+## 2. Bytes per position and per trajectory
+
+| Output | Positions recorded | Per position | 16K trajectory | 200K trajectory | 1M trajectory |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | all | 384 B / 392 B (MoE layers × top-k × 1 B) | 6.3 MB | 80 MB | 411 MB |
+| top-k 256 | generated only | 2 KB (256 × (int32 id + fp32 logprob)) | 17 MB | 42 MB | 215 MB |
+| top-p mask (≤ 256 ids) | generated only | ≤ 1 KB | 8.4 MB | 21 MB | 107 MB |
+| indexer, 12 layers × 2048 | all | 96 KiB | 1.6 GB | 20 GB | 103 GB |
+| indexer, 61 layers × 2048 | all | 488 KiB | 8.2 GB | 102 GB | 524 GB |
+
+The two indexer rows assume a model of the same size with a DSA-style indexer. Bounding the top-p mask at 256 ids requires `top_k ≤ 256` at sampling time.
+
+## 3. Cache segment as a KV layer: host memory
+
+Only outputs recorded at every position need a cache segment (R3, indexer); top-k and mask cover generated positions, which are never prefix hits. The cache segment's token capacity equals the full-attention KV capacity.
+
+| Output | Single node, per engine (589K tokens) | Single node, per node (8 engines) | Frontier, per replica (12.8M tokens) | Ratio to KV (single node / frontier) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | 0.23 GB | 1.8 GB | 5.0 GB | 0.39% / 1.06% |
+| indexer, 12 layers | 58 GB | 463 GB | 1.26 TB | 100% / 267% |
+| indexer, 61 layers | 294 GB | 2.35 TB | 6.4 TB | 508% / 1356% |
+
+At frontier scale each replica has ≈51 × 200K ≈ 10.4M live tokens, 81% of its 12.8M capacity. R3's cache segment is cheap; an uncompressed indexer cache segment exceeds host memory.
+
+## 4. Delivery pool
+
+Pool size = per-node in-flight bytes ÷ 0.75 (in-flight cap at 75%).
+
+| Output | Single node: in flight | Single node: pool | Frontier: per node in flight | Frontier: cluster in flight | Frontier: per-node pool (512K start / 1M bound) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | 1.6 GB | 4.3 GB | 4.1 GB | 8.8 TB | 14 / 28 GB |
+| top-k 256 | 4.3 GB | 11.5 GB | 2.1 GB | 4.6 TB | 7 / 15 GB |
+| top-p mask | 2.1 GB | 5.6 GB | 1.1 GB | 2.3 TB | 3.6 / 7.3 GB |
+| indexer, 12 layers | 206 GB | 1.1 TB | 1.0 TB | 2.2 PB | 3.5 / 7.0 TB |
+| indexer, 61 layers | 1.0 TB | 5.6 TB | 5.2 TB | 11.3 PB | 18 / 36 TB |
+
+Deduplication across turns is mandatory at frontier scale. Rewriting the full context every turn would write ~2 GB of R3 for a 200K, 50-turn trajectory, 25× the deduplicated 80 MB.
+
+## 5. Write traffic and object counts (frontier scale)
+
+| Output | Cluster bandwidth | Per inference node | Object (16-position block) | Live objects (cluster) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | 3.3 GB/s | 1.5 MB/s | 6.3 KB | 1.4B |
+| top-k 256 | 1.7 GB/s | 0.8 MB/s | 33 KB | 141M |
+| top-p mask | 0.87 GB/s | 0.4 MB/s | 16 KB | 141M |
+| indexer, 12 layers | 831 GB/s | 385 MB/s | 1.6 MB | 1.4B |
+| indexer, 61 layers | 4.2 TB/s | 1.96 GB/s | 8.0 MB | 1.4B |
+
+Bandwidth is not the constraint for R3, top-k or mask. Object count is:
+- 16-position objects mean ~530K objects/s, more than a single Mooncake master handles unbatched (54K objects/s measured).
+- Larger blocks (64–256 tokens), one object per block holding every output kind, and batched puts (337K objects/s with batches of 16) bring this within budget.
+
+## 6. Training side: reads per step
+
+A frontier-scale step consumes ≈33K trajectories (41/s × 807 s) across ≈465 training nodes. With pipeline parallelism, each stage reads only its own layers of R3 and indexer; top-k and mask are read by the last stage only.
+
+| Output | Single node: per step | Frontier: per training node per step |
+|---|---|---|
+| R3 | 3.2 GB | 5.8 GB |
+| top-k 256 | 8.6 GB | 3.0 GB |
+| top-p mask | 4.3 GB | 1.5 GB |
+| indexer, 12 layers | 825 GB | 1.4 TB |
+| indexer, 61 layers | 4.2 TB | 7.3 TB |
+
+## 7. Recomputing in-flight work at weight sync
+
+```
+per-replica in-flight tokens × 2 × 23B active params / (4 GPUs × 5 PFLOPS FP8 × 40% MFU)
+= 51 × 200K × 46 GFLOP / 8 PFLOPS ≈ 60 s
+```
+
+That is ≈7.4% of each 807 s interval (MLP only; attention adds more). Frontier-scale runs therefore keep generating across weight versions and reuse older KV rather than recomputing in-flight requests. Prefix hits on blocks computed by an older version are normal.
+
+## 8. Constraints on the design
+
+- R3 and top-k are the same order of magnitude (2–4 GB in flight per node, 7–28 GB pools) and can share one delivery protocol. Top-k needs no cache segment.
+- A cache segment in a KV layer is affordable for R3, but not for an uncompressed indexer.
+- The indexer needs its own treatment: compression, a subset of layers or positions, or an SSD tier.
+- Deduplication is mandatory at frontier scale, and release must be per trajectory: trajectories span many weight versions, so deleting by generation is not possible.
+- With BI on, row differences between computations come only from weight-version changes, except for the cases in the [experiments](experiments.md). Rows must stay tied to the KV that produced them.
+
+## 9. Scenario coverage vs. existing systems
+
+Compared with the SGLang output store and Miles (which reject several of these configurations at startup), the protocol explicitly handles:
+- multimodal prompts: positions counted on the engine-side expanded sequence, and image hashes included in the prefix hash;
+- multiple policies or LoRAs sharing an engine: a new session per policy and in-flight caps per policy;
+- streaming responses: references are returned in the final chunk;
+- chat-message APIs: the engine-side `prompt_token_ids` are returned;
+- tool-observation positions: explicit fill values, so an empty support set never yields NaN losses;
+- training-step retry and checkpoint rollback: release only after the step commits, and regenerate after a rollback;
+- offline saving of rollouts: read inline first;
+- MoE backends that bypass top-k: reject R3 at startup;
+- routers that drop unknown fields: a missing `aux` is an error;
+- requests aborted while queued: they produce an empty set of rows;
+- leak checks at job end: a sweep that reports the count.
+
+## 10. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, measured
+
+Model (public config):
+- 40 layers + 3 MTP layers;
+- 384 experts, top-6;
+- 8 indexer source layers, top-512.
+
+Setup: TP4 + EP4, BI on. The frontier column keeps the workload from section 1 and swaps in DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash per-token sizes.
+
+| Output | Positions | Per position | 200K trajectory | Frontier: per replica in flight (≈10.4M positions) | Frontier: per-replica pool (÷0.75) |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| R3 | all | 480 B (40 × 6 × uint16) | 96 MB | 5.0 GB | 6.7 GB |
+| top-k 256 | generated | 2 KB | 41 MB | 2.1 GB | 2.8 GB |
+| hidden (`lm_head` input, fp8 + per-token scale) | generated | ≈5 KB (hidden 5120) | 102 MB | 5.2 GB | 7.0 GB |
+| indexer, raw (8 × 512 × int32) | all | 16 KB | 3.3 GB | 170 GB | 227 GB |
+| indexer, 20-bit + zstd (measured) | all | 2.5–3.6 KB | 0.5–0.7 GB | 26–37 GB | 35–50 GB |
+
+- **KV capacity, measured.** A TP4 engine at 0.65 GPU memory utilization holds 3.39M tokens.
+  - R3 as a block-row cache (or KV layer): ≈1.6 GB per engine, ~1% of the KV.
+  - Indexer: ≈54 GB raw, ≈10 GB compressed.
+- **Indexer compression.** Selections are bitwise reproducible under BI. Compressed, the indexer is 5–7× R3, and fits in the same delivery pool.
+- **Hidden states.** fp8 hidden times the teacher's `lm_head` is within full-vocabulary KL < 1e-3 of vLLM's distribution. The behavior logprob must still come from the inline per-token logprob, because recomputed logits are not bitwise equal.
